This program was written by Steve Simon on 2026-05-22 and is placed in the public domain. The program will read in several different publicly available data sets and produce a few simple tables and graphs. I hope to include some of these in my book.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: setup

library(glue)
library(gt)
library(stringr)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Chapter 10 

This chapter will use the famous Titanic data set. I have a [copy][ref-simon-nodate1] on my github site, but you can find it many other places as well. I wrote a [simple data dictionary][ref-simon-nodate2] for this file.

[ref-simon-nodate1]: https://github.com/pmean/data/blob/main/files/titanic.txt
[ref-simon=nodate2]: https://github.com/pmean/data/blob/main/files/titanic.yaml

```{r}
#| label: ch10-read

ti <- read_tsv(file="../data/titanic.txt")
glimpse(ti)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: ch10-summary

table_10_01 <- summary(ti$Age)

table_10_01
```

We could use

```{}
sum(is.na(ti$Age))
```

or 

```{}
count_missing <- list(~ sum(is.na(.x)))
ti |> 
  summarise(across(everything(), count_missing))
```

If we wanted to show a Python example, we could use

```{}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ti = pd.read_csv("../data/titanic.csv")
table_10_01_py = ti['survived'].isnull().sum()

table_10_01_py
```



Use

```{}
ti['Survived'].value_counts()
```


```{r}
#| label: ch10-save

save(
  table_10_01,
  file="../data/chapter-10-output.RData")
```
